summary: Shipped `src/authoring-preview/` — a fast authoring preview that serves the immutable Recon Template plus authored Site state and lightweight theme/asset overlays, with NO build, NO asset copy and NO production package per edit. Architecture: a patched COPY of the template app (two guarded, anchored patches in the src/production/patch.ts style, dead unless WR_AUTHORING_HOT=1) built ONCE, run behind one stable-URL proxy. Content invalidation is an authoring EPOCH read from its own env var WR_AUTHORING_EPOCH_FILE — a tiny file whose entire CONTENT is a monotonic token written AFTER the overlay, which closes the prototyper's named (mtimeMs,size) collision hole and keeps `process.env.WR_SLOT_VALUES_FILE` from appearing twice (the prototype's other named defect). Theme rides the pure `generateThemeOverlay` into an mtime-gated stylesheet append; images ride the EXISTING per-request media read in the proxy, plus the two things that made it dead in a browser: no-store in authoring mode and byte-sniffed content type. The editor bridge is spliced before </head> of HTML responses only (never into RSC flight), posts to each editor origin explicitly (never "*"), validates origin AND event.source AND protocol tag, and reports the existing data-wr-node / data-wr-dyn-node plus route/viewport/pageId — no data-wr-slot invented. MEASURED IN A REAL BROWSER, 6 reps each: text 144 ms median / 150 max, url 138/153, theme 71/79, image 5/7, warm preview start 617/627; one-time cold materialize (copy+patch+next build) 3275/3335 (n=3); the avoided baseline, a real production compile of the same lineage, 3759/4049 (n=3, 77 MB build dir). 0 browser runtime errors, 0 hydration errors, 0 `[wr-slot]` guard warnings everywhere. Inertness proven twice: 19/19 routes byte-identical to the PRISTINE template app after normalizing only Next's own build identity (max raw delta 1 char), and a new overlay+epoch changes nothing in a server started without the flag. A REAL production package baked after the preview session contains the bridge 0 times, the patch marker 0 times, WR_AUTHORING_EPOCH_FILE 0 times, and the template run is byte-untouched. New suite scripts/smoke-authoring-preview.ts: 41 checks / 0 failures / ~25 s, with two checks proven falsifiable by deliberate sabotage and exact restore. src/production/patch.ts was NOT touched; package.json was NOT edited; zero git mutations.

items.evidence: NEW MODULE src/authoring-preview/ (8 files), placed as a sibling of the other serve-boundary owners (src/theme, src/seo, src/assets) because it IS one. preview = immutable Recon Template + authored Site state + lightweight theme/asset overlays. materialize.ts copies <templateRun>/app into data/<host>/authoring-previews/<previewId>/app, applies patch.ts's two anchored patches and runs `next build` ONCE; the reuse key is patchVersion + templateId + the sha256 of the two PRISTINE runtime files, so a recompiled template or a changed patch forces a rebuild rather than serving a stale app. workspace.ts owns the mutable layer (slot-values.json, authoring-epoch, theme-overlay.css, media/ overrides) with atomic write+rename. serve.ts is the single stable-URL proxy; session.ts is the API. The template run is a READ-ONLY input and is byte-checked untouched (28.P3.37, 39 files). Measured warm start 617 ms median / 627 max (n=6) — the whole startAuthoringPreview call plus the first page actually served, nothing excluded. src/recon-template/parity-qa.ts was EXTENDED, not broken: RunningApp gained `output: () => string` (line 129/170) so the preview can assert 0 `[wr-slot]` warnings; every existing field and caller is unchanged and the 5 suites reaching parity-qa still pass at their prior counts.

An authored.slotValues edit is one atomic overlay write plus one epoch write. 28.P3.11 asserts the new value is served on the FIRST request after the write (attempts===1); 28.P3.12 that the baseline contained none of it and the bound occurrences did change; 28.P3.14 that reverting to defaults restores the served bytes EXACTLY (byte equality against the pre-edit document — the expectedValue guard round-trips); 28.P3.31 that it is visible in a REAL browser. Requirement-1's negative half is asserted, not assumed: 28.P3.15 .next/BUILD_ID mtime never moved across every edit, 28.P3.16 no new production-builds and no new asset-materializations directory appeared, 28.P3.17 workerStarts()===1. Measured browser-visible 144 ms median / 150 max (n=6, timer starts BEFORE the write, no server pre-warm); server-side first-request 54 ms median / 75 max (n=6).

A url slot goes through the identical path (it is an attribute binding, guarded on expectedValue the same way). 28.P3.13 asserts the served HTML carries `href="<new value>"` — not merely the string somewhere, which would pass on a substitution proxy that corrupted an unrelated occurrence. Measured browser-visible (Playwright waiting for a[href="…"] to be attached) 138 ms median / 153 max (n=6).

authored.theme tokens go through lineage.ts authoredThemeOverlayCss → src/theme/overlay.ts generateThemeOverlay — the SAME pure function themeStageRunner calls, so the CSS is byte-identical to what the stage would produce, not an approximation; the expensive half of that stage is writing a run directory, which a preview needs none of. serve.ts re-reads the overlay file whenever its (mtime,size) moves instead of freezing it into a Buffer at construction (the shipped bug in src/theme/serve.ts:64). 28.P3.26 asserts the browser's computed --wr-theme-color-accent-primary changes with NO navigation and workerStarts()===1; 28.P3.27 that BUILD_ID did not move. Measured browser-visible via a <link> swap 71 ms median / 79 max (n=6). The served HTML is byte-identical by construction, so this path cannot affect hydration.

Uses the EXISTING hot seam rather than a new one: serve.ts serves /media/<name> by a per-request readFile, override directory first and the FROZEN materialization second — no media set is copied, one authored replacement is one file write. Two changes make it actually work in a browser: `cache-control: no-store, must-revalidate` in authoring mode (28.P3.30; the shipped src/assets/serve.ts sends `immutable`) and a content type sniffed from the override's BYTES (28.P3.7) because the media name carries the ORIGINAL extension and an operator replacing a .webp with a PNG is ordinary. 28.P3.28 asserts source asset URLs were rewritten to /media paths; 28.P3.29 asserts the RENDERED PIXEL changed — a 1x1 canvas readback returning exactly 200,10,40 — with no navigation, workerStarts()===1 and BUILD_ID unmoved. Measured 5 ms median / 7 max (n=6). lineage.ts loadMaterializationLineage composes the materialization manifest (inventoryId → sourceUrl) with the rewrite map (sourceUrl → /media/<sha>.<ext>) so an authored.assets assetId resolves to the media names it is served at.

src/authoring-preview/bridge.ts renders one <script> spliced before </head> of text/html responses ONLY — never into an RSC flight payload, which React parses as data — following the shipped src/seo/serve.ts head-splice precedent. 28.P3.21 asserts injection in the actual served bytes. Security is asserted structurally AND behaviourally: 28.P3.8 asserts the source never contains postMessage(message, "*"), does contain the origin allowlist test and `event.source !== window.parent && event.source !== window.opener`, addresses [data-wr-node],[data-wr-dyn-node], and contains NO data-wr-slot; 28.P3.22/23 drive a real cross-origin editor harness (its own port) that receives `ready` and a `pong` echoing its own token; 28.P3.24 drives a SECOND harness on a non-allowlisted origin which receives NOTHING at all and whose ping is ignored. 28.P3.25 asserts hover AND click report a real node id matching /^n\d+$/, a dynNode field, route === "/blog", viewport === "desktop" and a pageId — i.e. exactly the Slot V2 addressing context (pageId, viewport, nodeId) the editor needs to invert slot-bindings.json, with no new DOM attribute. Inbound commands: ping, describe-selection, refresh-styles, refresh-media, reload.

Proven by baking, not by argument. §7 of the suite runs the REAL runProductionCompile on the same lineage AFTER the full preview session (materialize + text/url/theme/image edits + browser drive) and walks every file of the produced package: 198 files, 22,042,083 bytes, bridge marker 0, authoring patch marker 0, WR_AUTHORING_EPOCH_FILE 0 (28.P3.34/35/36), and the template run byte-compares identical before and after (28.P3.37). Independently reproduced across 3 further compiles (tmp/wr28/preview-scratch/bench2.ts, runs 2026-08-27T12-13-10-354Z / 12-13-14-490Z / 12-13-18-332Z): 0/0/0 each. The structural reason is separation, not a flag: the preview patches a COPY under authoring-previews/ and the production compiler copies the immutable template run. src/production/patch.ts was NOT modified, and the epoch deliberately uses its own env var so `process.env.WR_SLOT_VALUES_FILE` occurs exactly as many times in the patched file as in the pristine one (28.P3.3) — the prototype defect the recon named.

Real Chromium throughout. Errors collected from BrowserContext 'console' (type error), BrowserContext 'weberror' AND Page 'pageerror', classified with the same /hydrat|minified react error #(418|423|425)/i rule src/recon-template/parity-qa.ts uses. ACTUAL COUNTS: benchmark session (6 reloads + 6 stylesheet swaps + 6 media swaps + hover/click) → 0 runtime errors, 0 hydration errors, 0 `[wr-slot]` warnings; smoke suite 28.P3.32/33 → 0 and 0; linear.app canary 28.P3.41 → 0 and 0. Also 28.P3.18 asserts 0 `[wr-slot]` applier guard warnings across every content edit. Nothing was reported-and-left: no hydration error was ever observed with this design, and the reason is structural — the bridge is the only added markup and it is spliced exactly where the already-shipped SEO proxy splices, the theme path changes no HTML at all, and the content path re-renders server-side so the SSR HTML and the flight payload always agree.

The smallest safe refresh architecture: overlay indirection, two anchored patches, nothing on the client, and no reconstruction / template compile / theme run / asset materialization / production bake in any edit path. Asserted negatively (28.P3.15 BUILD_ID mtime unmoved, 28.P3.16 no new production-builds or asset-materializations dir, 28.P3.17 workerStarts()===1) and measured positively: text 54 ms server-side / 144 ms browser vs a real production compile of the same lineage at 3759 ms median (n=3) producing a 77.4 MB build directory and a 22.0 MB package. INERTNESS proven twice so the production path is provably unaffected: 28.P3.19 — with WR_AUTHORING_HOT unset the patched app is byte-identical to the PRISTINE template app on all 19 routes after normalizing ONLY Next's own build identity (buildId, chunk file names, webpack module ids), max raw byte delta 1 character; 28.P3.20 — writing a new overlay + epoch changes NOTHING in that same non-hot server, i.e. the documented process-lifetime memoization is intact. The Task-17.1 portal blind spot the prototyper listed as an open risk is now closed: 28.P3.38/39/40 hot-edit a dynamic-template binding on the real linear.app template and a real browser click mounts the portal menu showing the new value, 0 guard warnings, 0 hydration errors.

limitations: EVERY EDIT-LATENCY NUMBER IS ONE MACHINE AND ONE SITE: darwin 25.2.0 / APFS / Node 22 / next 16.3.0 / headless chromium / 127.0.0.1, on domainchecker.co.kr (19 routes, 1957 slots, 4832 bindings, largest page JSON 292 KB), with other Task-28 phases running concurrently on the same box. The linear.app template (8 routes, 2441 text slots, 1.4 MB home page JSON) was exercised for CORRECTNESS only — I did not run the 6-rep benchmark there, so I hold NO measured edit latency for a large page and do not claim one.

EVERY EDIT METRIC IS A FULL-DOCUMENT NUMBER. A text or url edit re-parses the whole page JSON on the next request and the browser does a full reload. There is no partial, streaming or diff-based DOM update and no debouncing — an un-debounced keystroke-rate editor would re-parse per keystroke. I measured neither debouncing nor incremental update; that is Phase 4 work.

THE PREVIEW'S /media PATH IS NOT CONTENT-ADDRESSED. An authored image replacement is written to <preview>/overlay/media/<original-name>, so the preview serves different bytes at the frozen materialization's content hash. That is what makes the edit one file write instead of an assets-stage rerun, but it means the preview's media URL does not carry the guarantee the production artifact's does. The assets StageRunner still does the real re-hashed materialization at build time.

authored.assets IS CONSUMED THROUGH A MAPPING I BUILT, NOT THROUGH THE ASSETS STAGE. loadMaterializationLineage composes manifest (inventoryId → sourceUrl) with rewrite-map (sourceUrl → /media/<sha>.<ext>). The suite drives replaceMedia by the media names actually present in the rendered DOM, so the mapping runs and its rewrite map is what the proxy uses — but the assetId → mediaName step is not independently asserted by its own check. The site-level ids `og-image` / `organization-logo` have no inventory entry and therefore no preview media name at all.

authored.assets[*].alt STILL HAS NO CONSUMER, here as everywhere. The preview replaces BYTES; it writes no markup. An alt edit changes nothing in the preview, exactly as it changes nothing in the bake.

authored.brand IS NOT SURFACED IN THE PREVIEW AT ALL. Nothing in src/authoring-preview reads it. A REPLACE/REMOVE/PRESERVE decision is a bake-time IR rewrite owned by the parallel brand builder, so an operator cannot see the effect of a brand decision in this preview.

SEO IS NOT IN THE PREVIEW. The proxy does not rewrite <title>, does not splice the SEO head block and does not serve /robots.txt — src/seo/serve.ts still owns that and was deliberately not chained in. A preview shows the template's own titles, not the production plan's.

PAINT-TWIN AND SVG-TEXT BINDINGS WERE NOT DRIVEN THROUGH THE HOT CYCLE. The linear canary closes the dynamic-template / portal gap the Phase-2 prototyper named (28.P3.38/40, in a real browser), but linear carries only 4 paint-twin bindings and the domainchecker fixture has 0 paint-twin and 0 svg-text bindings, so neither surface is covered by a check. They traverse the same applySlotContent path — that is an argument, not evidence.

CONCURRENCY AND CAPACITY ARE UNMEASURED. One preview server, one browser, one editor. No multi-tenant memory figure, no simultaneous editors, and no test of two writers racing on the same overlay file — the epoch ordering makes a SINGLE writer safe and says nothing about two.

THE HOT SEAM IS PROCESS-LOCAL AND POLLED. slotContentEpoch is read per loadPage call (a ~1-byte file read); there is no watcher, no push and no cross-process invalidation. Two `next start` processes on the same preview dir would each hold their own epoch state — correct, but untested.

THE PREVIEW APP IS A FULL COPY OF THE TEMPLATE APP (~82 MB on disk for domainchecker, ~100 MB for linear, per template). The copy measured 49-70 ms on this APFS volume; on a filesystem without cheap clones it will cost materially more and I did not measure that.

THE PRODUCTION-BAKE BASELINE I MEASURED IS domainchecker's (3759 ms median, 77 MB). It is a small site; the last recorded linear.app bake in this program was ~36 s including the media copy. I did not re-measure linear's bake, so the 'cost avoided' figure quoted here is the SMALL-site figure and understates the gap on a large one.

NO CLI AND NO RELEASE-PROJECT ENTRYPOINT. startAuthoringPreview takes a template run dir plus authored values; it does not load a ReleaseProject and nothing in src/release calls it. Wiring authored.slotValues / authored.theme / authored.assets straight out of a release project is Phase 4 work.

package.json WAS NOT EDITED, per the program contract. The suite is registered only by the appended line in docs/result/handoffs/28-intel/pending-package-scripts.tsv; until an integrator applies it, `pnpm smoke:authoring-preview` does not exist and the suite must be run as `npx tsx scripts/smoke-authoring-preview.ts` through the mutex.

THE §8 LINEAR CANARY IS SKIPPABLE BY DESIGN (prints SKIP and drops 4 checks if the linear template run is deleted), following the smoke-regions §7 precedent. The suite reports 41 checks with the canary and would report 37 without; nothing asserts its own total — the same repo-wide gap the pre-overnight audit recorded.

REGRESSION SCOPE: I ran typecheck plus the FIVE suites that reach src/recon-template/parity-qa.ts (theme 47, assets 140, seo 97, content-injection 145, recon-template 109 — all 0 failures), found with `grep -rln parity-qa src scripts`, because that is the only shipped file outside my new module I touched. I did NOT run the other suites and hold no fresh evidence about them, so I make no claim about the full regression total. Note content-injection read 145 when I ran it, above the 138 Phase 2 recorded — another phase raised it concurrently; there is no negative delta anywhere I measured.

28.P3.29 KEPT PASSING UNDER SABOTAGE A (media header forced back to `immutable`). That is honest and worth carrying: a cache-bust query token defeats an immutable header for an img.src swap, so the no-store header is a belt-and-braces correctness property (it matters for a plain reload, which is how the recon measured the stale pixel) rather than the mechanism that makes the pixel change. 28.P3.30 asserts it separately for that reason.
